gaps.description: No function type in the doc. An invented `Validator` type wrapped in `maybe` is passed and called like an operation (`try check line`).

gaps.construct: errors from the callback and from fmt.Errorf propagated unchanged; formatted error message
gaps.description: `fails with` needs a closed list of names and failures carry no message. The callback's arbitrary errors collapse into one invented name InvalidLine and the 'missing validateFirstLine func' text is lost.

gaps.construct: line is a slice aliasing bufio's internal buffer; r.buf[:0] reuses storage; the copy exists only because the next read overwrites the alias
gaps.description: Scribe has values and editable parameters but no slices or borrows, so the aliasing hazard that motivates the copy cannot be expressed and the copy step becomes meaningless; zero-copy behaviour is not preserved.

gaps.construct: bufio.Reader.Buffered() and Peek(2) without consuming input
gaps.description: No buffered-reader vocabulary in the doc; `buffered_count of` and `peek_bytes n from` are declared as invented operations on a BufferedReader capability.
The doc names a `Bytes` type but has no byte type, byte literal or byte indexing rule; constants newline_byte, return_byte, space_byte and a Byte type are assumed.

gaps.construct: append(r.buf, trim(line)...) - appending a slice to a byte buffer
gaps.description: `append value to items` adds one element; `followed by` joins sequences but is shown only in ensure lines. `followed by` is used in body `set` lines.

gaps.construct: for r.skipSpace() > 0 { ... } - a loop whose condition consumes input
gaps.description: An effectful call in a `repeat while` condition is not shown, and there is no `repeat forever`; a never-changing `more` flag plus `stop` is used, and a `decreases` measure had to be derived from the size limit.

gaps.construct: method on *Reader that reads and mutates r.buf and uses r.R
gaps.description: Receiver becomes an editable parameter. `uses r of reader` names a capability that is a field of a parameter, which no example shows.

gaps.construct: after the nil check, validateFirstLine is used as non-nil later in the body
gaps.description: There is no flow-sensitive narrowing; a value unwrapped in a `when some` branch cannot be kept outside the branch, so the maybe is opened twice with an unreachable `nothing` branch.
No sized integers or limit constants in the doc; `max_int64` is assumed and conversions are implicit in the translation, which the doc forbids but gives no explicit form for.
Deliberately discarding a failure has no form; the invented peek_bytes is declared as not failing, which hides that the original drops an error.

doc_rules_contradicted: No implicit conversions. (int64(len(r.buf)) comparisons are written as plain Int/Nat comparisons because the doc has no explicit conversion form)
invented_syntax: Validator type and calling a parameter as an operation (`try check line`)
uses r of reader (capability that is a field of a parameter)
buffered_count of / peek_bytes n from (buffered reader operations)
newline_byte, return_byte, space_byte, Byte type, max_int64
X followed by Y in body expressions
is_ascii_letter (item 0 of peek) - call with a parenthesised argument
notes: This protocol-reading function is mostly expressible, but its whole performance design (peek to avoid a copy, slices that alias a buffer, reusing buf storage) is invisible in Scribe, so a faithful translation is semantically right but loses the reason the code exists. Callback parameters and open error sets recur here as in F04 and F16. The `decreases` requirement on `repeat while` is awkward for input-driven loops whose termination depends on the stream ending.
